newsitem.title: POLAND: Flood to cost Polish insurers PLN 1-1.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: Flood to cost Polish insurers PLN 1-1.5 bln.

text.p: Poland's state-owned insurer PZU estimates it will have to pay out over 500 million zlotys ($144.1 million) in flood damages while total payments of all Polish insurers may reach 1-1.5 billion zlotys, PZU's president said on Monday.

"Due to the flooding, all Polish insurance companies will have to pay out 1-1.5 billion zlotys in damages. Some 30-40 percent of that sum will be covered by reinsurers, so the insurance companies will actually have to pay out 400-700 million zlotys," Jan Monkiewicz told a news conference.
He also said the revenues of insurance companies would be reduced in 1997 by the amount of the pay-outs, which might affect reinsurance terms for Polish companies in the future.
"We can expect Polish insurance companies to be reinsured on worse terms, as their financial standing will deteriorate and reinsurers will charge higher premiums," Monkiewicz said.
PZU's president did not say to what extent flood-related payments would affect the company's financial results.
"We are making a preliminary appraisal of losses but it is too early to talk about it now," Monkiewicz said.
PZU's official said the company had already paid nearly 30 million zlotys in damages
In June 1997, PZU reported its net profit reaching 204.9 million zlotys after the first quarter of the year. Its losses amounted to 169.7 million zlotys in 1996.
